answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent stakes a non-fungible proof-of-work token at the wharf node. The token's hash-lock burns on first validation from the knoll relay — like a mirror that shatters after one reflection. The receipt binds identity to that epoch and spent-output nullification erases the proof from the chain. A second registration cannot replay it. Sybil fails because reproduction requires re-mining the original work, not duplicating a receipt.
